title: Hand-made sharding with postgres_fdw
caption: Core Postgres has no built-in sharding, so you build it by hand: a coordinator prunes a partitioned table and postgres_fdw sends SQL to shard servers, while a replica only copies everything for reads.

badges.meaning: Client connects through a pooler (outside core)
Pooler forwards SQL to the coordinator
Coordinator asks pruning which partitions can match, using the partition bounds
Pruning keeps only the surviving foreign scans for postgres_fdw
postgres_fdw sends Remote SQL to the shard servers
Optional streaming replica receives WAL to scale reads

title: One query, one shard
caption: A SELECT for region eu and id 5 is pruned to one partition, so only Shard 1 gets Remote SQL and Shard 2 is never contacted.

badges.meaning: Client sends the SELECT to the coordinator
Planner prunes partitions (partprune.c) and keeps orders_s1
postgres_fdw writes the remote SQL string (deparse.c)
Remote SQL is sent to Shard 1
postgres_fdw passes rows to the coordinator
Coordinator returns the result to the client

title: Partition tree in memory
caption: The coordinator keeps three small structs about the partitioned table, and the oids[] array in PartitionDescData points to the child tables that pruning picks from.

badges.meaning: PartitionKeyData: how the table is split (strategy and key column)
PartitionDescData: the list of child table OIDs
PartitionBoundInfoData: the sorted bounds of each child
Child partitions, here foreign tables on two shards
